scope: Audited public static-fetch and hosted virtual-shell boundaries; not whole-image safety or deployment approval
audit: safeFetch, downloadFile, fetch and document guarded bytes remain identical to v2.11.704/705. Undici and ipaddr versions and the complete Undici lib tree remain identical.

Changed engine selection routes X/Twitter pages exclusively through Exchange and fails closed when unavailable. The Exchange URL remains unset by the required configuration predicate; caller URLs do not select an alternate transport.
PDF changes add reserved-capacity processing restrictions and errors, rather than a new direct transport. Both US-only and reserved-capacity failures avoid fallback.
Exchange eligibility and feedback response logging changed; the Exchange configured URL and secret still gate these calls. types.js changes add error/schema definitions.

Hosted /v2/bash is enabled by default. It executes a just-bash virtual filesystem in a separate bounded process, with an empty OS environment, four concurrent shells, a deadline, RSS watchdog and command allowlist. It does not invoke an OS bash shell.

The built-in Firecrawl command calls this API using the socket local address and port, not the caller Host header. Only fixed search/scrape routes are called, preserving their validation. Inline API-key flags are refused.

Docs requests use the fixed docs.firecrawl.dev origin and matching index links; they use normal fetch, including its redirect handling. This audit does not claim arbitrary docs-origin compromise protection.

Syntax fingerprints cover all 11 original files and 11 additional entry/config/helper files. Comments and positions are ignored; executable AST changes, ASI, directives, regexp flags and tagged template raw strings remain significant.

The full just-bash runtime dependency graph is pinned from the actual shell-worker resolution context: 77 packages and 3545 files, including external sprintf-js, same-name npm/builtin packages (string_decoder and buffer), optional-dependency absence and lazy-loaded commands. Nested dependency shadows and undeclared root dependencies fail closed. The independently exported closure SHA256 and graph digest matched in PC WSL. New package content requires qualification. This record is an audited baseline, not a release-version selection restriction.

The fork local monitor judge source and socket adapter remain on fork main; the currently deployed core image has no local judge adapter or configured judge socket. The separate monitor service remains an independent deployment.
validation: PC WSL Node 22.22.1 parsed the actual candidate compiled files; export SHA256 matched the GA401 read-only export.

Eleven syntax admission/parser regressions passed in PC WSL, including ASI, directives, regexp flags, tagged templates, nonfinite numeric values, legacy-profile shell bypass rejection, external transitive package mutation, worker-local resolution, dependency/config mismatch and complete extra-helper coverage.

Eight hosted-shell tests passed in PC WSL against the actual compiled worker and just-bash 3.6.0: text pipeline, host-file isolation, parent environment isolation, network/runtime tool exclusion, fresh filesystem, credential-flag rejection, cancellation and bounded output.
